summary: Frontend-only testing of the 'Selected Work' ProjectRail (next/prev, mouse drag, keyboard, mobile touch, page overflow) on /rail-preview and /. DEFINITIVE FINDING: the rail component logic is CORRECT and every interaction works when the Next.js dev server is hit directly (http://localhost:3000), but on the PUBLIC preview URL the React app NEVER HYDRATES (no __reactFiber on any element), so nothing on ANY page is interactive - buttons, drag, dots all dead. This is an environment/serving problem (Next 16 dev server behind the preview ingress: HMR WebSocket wss://.../_next/webpack-hmr returns 502/404 and Cloudflare injects scripts/iframe into <body>), not a bug in ProjectRail.tsx. One real component bug found: keyboard arrow navigation never works because the keydown listener is on .work-rail__viewport while the prev/next buttons live OUTSIDE it (.work-rail__head), and the viewport itself is not focusable.

ui_bugs.issue: ArrowRight/ArrowLeft do NOT change the active project. Verified on localhost (hydrated): focus work-rail-next + ArrowRight -> counter stays 01; click inside .work-rail__viewport + ArrowRight -> counter stays 01; only a synthetic keydown dispatched directly on .work-rail__viewport moves it (01->02). Root cause: keydown listener is attached to .work-rail__viewport (ProjectRail.tsx L75-89) but the nav buttons are in .work-rail__head, a SIBLING of the viewport, so events never bubble to it; the viewport has no tabIndex so it can never receive focus either. Fix: attach the keydown handler on the outer .work-rail container (or window when the rail is in view), and/or add tabIndex={0} to the viewport.

integration_issues.flow: Entire site on public preview URL (hydration)
integration_issues.issue: On https://48f155bf-...preview.emergentagent.com/rail-preview AND / the SSR HTML renders but React hydration never completes: Object.keys(document.querySelector('[data-testid=work-rail-next]')) === [] (no __reactFiber$/__reactProps$). Reproduced 4/4 fresh loads + homepage. Consequence: NEXT click -> counter stays '01' and is-active stays work-card-makemytrip; PREV stays disabled; mouse drag does nothing (track transform:none, first card not even centered because the layout-effect centering never ran); dots dead. Same page on http://localhost:3000 hydrates within ~2s and everything works. Only console errors on public: repeated "WebSocket connection to 'wss://.../_next/webpack-hmr?id=...' failed: Error during WebSocket handshake: Unexpected response code: 502" (verbatim). curl WS-upgrade to the public /_next/webpack-hmr returns HTTP/2 404 while the same upgrade on localhost:3000 succeeds/hangs open. HTML diff local vs public shows Cloudflare additionally injects an inline challenge script + hidden <iframe> into <body>. All 21 JS chunks return 200, no pageerror, no CSP header.

action_items: PRIMARY: Stop serving the preview from `next dev`. Build and run production (`next build` then `next start -p 3000 -H 0.0.0.0`) so no HMR WebSocket is required; the dev-mode client runtime is what blocks hydration behind the ingress (ws upgrade to /_next/webpack-hmr returns 502/404 publicly). Then re-verify the rail on the public URL.

SECONDARY: supervisor 'frontend' program is broken - /var/log/supervisor/frontend.err.log repeats "supervisor: couldn't chdir to /app/frontend: ENOENT". The Next server is currently a manually-started `npm exec next dev -p 3000` (pid 3683) and will not survive a restart. Point the supervisor program at /app.
Fix keyboard navigation: move the keydown listener to the .work-rail root (or add tabIndex={0} to .work-rail__viewport) so ArrowLeft/ArrowRight work when the nav buttons or the rail have focus.
critical_code_review_comments: ProjectRail.tsx L75-89: keydown listener on viewportRef can never fire from the nav buttons (different subtree) and the viewport is not focusable -> the documented 'use arrow keys' aria-label is misleading; a11y/keyboard support is effectively dead.
Rail logic itself is sound: measure()/goTo()/snapFromDrag() all behave correctly (verified index 01-04, disabled states, velocity snap in both directions, dot jump).
No app-code change is needed for the reported 'swipe not working' symptom - it is a hydration/serving issue on the preview URL.

success_rate.frontend: 0% on public preview URL (nothing hydrates); 90% on localhost:3000 (9/10 checks pass, keyboard arrows fail)

test_credentials: None required; /app/memory exists but no credentials needed for this static site
context_for_next_testing_agent: Observed values, localhost:3000/rail-preview (hydrated): INITIAL 01/work-card-makemytrip; NEXT#1 02/work-card-spectra; NEXT#2 03/work-card-startup-india; PREV 02/work-card-spectra; prev disabled at 01 = True; next disabled at 04 (work-card-spec-ads) = True; mouse drag left 320px -> 02; drag right 320px -> 01; dot[3] click -> 04; mobile 390px: swipe left -> 02, NEXT -> 03, no page overflow (documentElement.scrollWidth 390 == innerWidth 390, body 390); desktop home scrollWidth 1920 == innerWidth 1920; homepage #work rail NEXT -> 02/work-card-spectra. Same script on the PUBLIC URL: counter frozen at 01 everywhere, elements have no React fiber. Use the hydration probe `Object.keys(el).some(k=>k.startsWith('__react'))` as the first check after any fix, and always retest on the PUBLIC URL, not localhost.
rca_of_the_issue: Repro: open the public preview URL, wait 6s, evaluate Object.keys(document.querySelector('[data-testid="work-rail-next"]')) -> [] (no React fiber) and clicking NEXT leaves .work-rail__count b at '01'. Same steps on http://localhost:3000 -> fiber present, counter goes 01->02. Difference is only the serving path: the app runs `next dev` (Next 16.2.6 + turbopack) and its client dev runtime repeatedly fails to open wss://<public>/_next/webpack-hmr (handshake 502; plain curl upgrade returns 404), i.e. the preview ingress/Cloudflare does not proxy WebSockets; hydration of the app root therefore never completes (only the nextjs-devtools portal appears) while the SSR HTML stays visible and inert. Cloudflare also injects an inline challenge script + hidden iframe into <body> on the public response, which can additionally break React 19 body hydration. Mitigation: serve a production build (next build + next start) for the preview instead of the dev server, and re-run the rail interaction tests on the public URL.
